nodes.summary: There is a closed connected topological 4-manifold $M$ that is aspherical, meaning that for every $k \ge 2$ and every point $x \in M$ the homotopy group $\pi_k(M, x)$ is trivial, and that is an integer homology 4-sphere, meaning that for every $k \ge 0$ the integral singular homology $H_k(M; \mathbb{Z})$ is isomorphic to $H_k(S^4; \mathbb{Z})$, where $S^4$ is the unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^5$.
nodes.title: Existence of an aspherical integer homology 4-sphere

nodes.summary: A closed topological 4-manifold is a nonempty, compact, connected, Hausdorff, second-countable topological space $M$ together with an atlas of charts covering $M$, each a homeomorphism from an open subset of $M$ onto an open subset of $\mathbb{R}^4$ (charts are modelled on all of $\mathbb{R}^4$, not on a half-space, so $M$ has no boundary).
nodes.title: Closed topological 4-manifold

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k$ and a topological space $X$, $H_k(X; \mathbb{Z})$ is the $k$-th singular homology of $X$ with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}$, viewed as a $\mathbb{Z}$-module.
nodes.title: Integral singular homology as a $\mathbb{Z}$-module

nodes.summary: A closed topological 4-manifold $M$ is aspherical if for every $k \ge 2$ and every point $x \in M$ the homotopy group $\pi_k(M, x)$ is trivial.
nodes.title: Aspherical closed 4-manifold

nodes.summary: A closed topological 4-manifold $M$ is an integer homology 4-sphere if for every $k \ge 0$ the integral singular homology $H_k(M; \mathbb{Z})$ is isomorphic, as a $\mathbb{Z}$-module, to $H_k(S^4; \mathbb{Z})$, where $S^4$ is the unit sphere in $\mathbb{R}^5$.
nodes.title: Integer homology 4-sphere
